title: Database Indexing
summary: Make the common lookup fast, then pay for it on writes.
keyPoints: An index is a second structure that speeds reads and adds work to every write.
B-trees serve equality, range, and sorted queries; hash indexes serve equality only.
Column order in a composite index decides which queries it can serve.
A predicate that matches few rows is a good index candidate; one that matches a large share often is not.
Read the query plan before and after adding an index.
Full-text and geospatial search need specialized indexes, often in a separate system.

complexity.note: A few page reads reach the key.

commonMistakes: Adding an index for every column instead of for a named query.
Putting the most selective column last in a composite index and expecting it to help.
Wrapping an indexed column in a function and expecting the index to be used.
Sending full-text search to the primary database when relevance and scale need a search system.
interviewNotes: List the queries first, then the indexes. Each index should have an owner query.
Mention the leftmost-prefix rule when you propose a composite index.
Say what the index costs: write amplification, storage, and cache pressure.
For search, say whether it lives in the database or a derived search index, and how it stays in sync.

checkYourself.question: Why can an index make writes slower?
checkYourself.answer: Every insert, update, or delete must also update each affected index. More indexes mean more pages to change, more log records, and more storage.

checkYourself.question: When does a composite index on (user_id, created_at) fail to help?
checkYourself.answer: When the query does not constrain user_id. The index is ordered by user_id first, so a query on created_at alone cannot use it as a range index.

checkYourself.question: Why might the planner ignore an index on a column that matches a large share of rows?
checkYourself.answer: Following the index and fetching many rows costs more than scanning the table once, so the planner chooses the cheaper plan.
